items.prompt: Make it emphatic: “We have rarely seen such demand.”
Make it emphatic: “Sales dropped and margins also shrank.”
Make it formal (no 'if'): “If we had known, we would have acted.”
Make it emphatic: “You must not open this file in any situation.”
Make it emphatic: “I have never seen such poor results.”
Make it emphatic: “The weather was so bad that the event was cancelled.”
Put the focus on the distributor: “The distributor caused the delay.”
Put the focus on what we need: “We need a clearer strategy.”
Put the focus on the reason: “We changed supplier because of the price.”
Put the focus on the time: “We only noticed the error on Friday.”
Past cause → present result: “I didn't take that job, so I'm not in Warsaw now.”
Present cause → past result: “He isn't careful, so he made that mistake.”
Make it formal (no 'if'): “If you need anything, just ask.”
Say it with 'but for': “Without the rebate, the deal would have collapsed.”
Report it: “People believe the CEO is about to resign.”
Report the past: “People say he left the company in 2019.”
Use 'have something done': “A specialist is repairing our server.”
Shorten it: “After we had reviewed the data, we changed the forecast.”
Shorten it: “When it is compared with last year, the result looks weak.”
Shorten it: “Because she didn't know the answer, she stayed silent.”
Make it formal with a noun: “When we implemented the system, costs fell.”
Make it formal with a noun: “Because demand increased, we hired more staff.”
Soften it: “This is the best solution.”
Soften it: “The new policy caused the drop in sales.”
Reply briefly: “Will the shipment arrive on time?” (you think it won't)
Avoid repetition: “If the client agrees, we'll sign; if the client doesn't agree, we'll renegotiate.”
Make it formal: “He must be informed — it's essential.”
Formal recommendation, no 'should': “The board said she ought to step down.”
Unreal past: “I want you to stop interrupting me.”
